question: Why can't dark matter be made of primordial black holes lighter than about 100 billion tonnes?
options: They would have evaporated long ago
They would have merged into heavier ones
Their Hawking glow would show in gamma rays
answer: Their Hawking glow would show in gamma rays. Only the lightest have finished evaporating; the survivors below 100 billion tonnes are still hot enough to shine. If they made up the dark matter, their combined gamma rays would outshine the background actually measured. Holes from there up to asteroid mass remain allowed.
move: Near a cut-off, look at what is still alive, not only at what died.
trap: Assuming the limit comes from holes that died, not ones still shining.
reference: Carr & Kühnel, Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter: Recent Developments, Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science, 2020
